capabilities.notes: Qoder CLI official ACP transport (qodercli --acp, protocolVersion 1), the default since 0.7.0; set HARNESS_SUPERVISOR_QODER_PROTOCOL=stream-json to use the legacy transport. Verified against real 1.1.82: initialize, session/new, session/load, session/prompt, session/cancel, Write approval through session/request_permission, and AskUserQuestion through elicitation/create when the client advertises elicitation.form. Permission modes map to ACP modes (bypass_permissions->yolo, accept_edits->acceptEdits, dont_ask->dontAsk, default->default, auto->auto); plan has no ACP equivalent and is rejected. Steering and queued follow-ups are not implemented: Qoder advertises promptQueueing in initialize._meta, but HS has not verified what a queued prompt does to run boundaries, so the HS session rejects a second prompt while one is active. Cancellation sends the session/cancel notification and responds to pending permissions/questions. ACP prompt results in 1.1.82 contain all-zero token counters, so Token usage is reported as unknown rather than zero. HS writes its own qoder-acp-session.json handle for resume; the conversation itself stays in Qoder's store. There is no sandbox: cwd is not a file-isolation boundary.

limits.usage: ACP prompt usage in Qoder 1.1.82 is all zeros; absence of run.usage events means unknown, not zero tokens.
limits.steering: ACP steer/follow-up are not implemented; capabilities report steer=false and followUp=false.
